newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends at new high, bonds firmer, dollar slips.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends at new high, bonds firmer, dollar slips.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks rallied to a record closing high in one of Wall Street's busiest days on Friday despite a proposed landmark settlement with U.S. state negotiators that depressed tobacco shares.
Bonds rose. The dollar fell as the British pound gained amid forecasts for higher British interest rates.

The Dow Jones industrial average finished up 19.45 points at 7,796.51, off its session high of 7,834. The close eclipsed the previous record of 7,782.04 set last Friday. For the week, the index rose 14.47 points.

But the rally was not broad-based, with losing issues outpacing gainers by a ratio of 1,479 to 1,101. About 652.7 million shares changed hands on the New York Stock Exchange in its third busiest day ever.
Traders said "triple witching" expirations of individual and index options and index futures skewed the day's results and bloated volume.
"A lot of it has to do with the options expiration," said Alice Hook, first vice president at McDonald & Co. "That's kind of creating a false tone."
Tobacco stocks, which rallied Thursday in anticipation of a liability settlement deal, turned lower after an agreement was reached shortly before the session's end.
The agreement would require cigarette companies to pay $368.5 billion over 25 years to compensate states and smokers and to fund programmes to help people quit smoking.

"It seems the industry was willing to give up a lot in order to get rid of the litigation," said Allan Kaplan, tobacco industry analyst at Merrill Lynch & Co. Inc. "This agreement seems like it should be able to make it through Congress."

Market players said a drop in long-term interest rates helped support stocks. The 30-year Treasury bond rose 7/32, or $2.19 on a $1,000 bond, reducing its yield to 6.66 percent from Thursday's close of 6.68 percent. The price and yield move in opposite directions. Earlier, the long bond yield fell as low as 6.64 percent -- a level not seen since Feb. 21.
The dollar rose to 1.7275 German marks from 1.7235 marks and 114.88 Japanese yen from 114.03 yen late Thursday.
Gasoline prices continued their recent downward slide as the market struggled to absorb high imports and record production.

At the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) gasoline for July delivery closed 0.61 cent lower at 55.48 cents a gallon after falling to a new life-of-contract low of 55.00 cents. July crude ended off 12 cents $18.55 a barrel. July heating oil ended 0.12 cent off at 51.33 cents a gallon.

Overseas, London's FTSE 100 closed at 4,593.9, down 59.8 points, or 1.29 percent, a loss of 189.2 points from last Friday. In Tokyo, the 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,385.54, down 122.31 points, or 0.60 percent. This was down 142.81 from last Friday.
